events.desc: Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT gathering of... talent. I must say, I happened to overhear — purely by accident, you understand — that the real treasure in this manor is hidden behind the old wood-burning stove in the kitchen. Something about a loose brick, third from the left, bottom row. I'd go myself, naturally, but I've a rather pressing appointment with the, ah, coat rack. Terribly important, coat racks. Don't all rush at once!
events.thinking:
Just arrived. The hollow behind my navel is already pulling — cataloguing. Coat rack, guest book, and... all these fools milling about in the entrance hall. Penelope, Peter Perfect, the Ant Hill Mob, even that snickering mutt Muttley. They're all here for the same thing I am, but none of them have the architecture for it. None of them think in sequences.

The guest book — that's interactive. Could have clues. But do I want to show my hand this early? No... better to let one of these simpletons do the reading while I watch what they find.

The library. Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription. An INSCRIPTION. That's where the treasure map is, or I'm not Reginald Foxworth. But if I go straight there, someone follows me. Better to send them the wrong way first.

I have this fake medal in my pocket. Useful for later — credentials, bribery, distraction. Keep it close.

The kitchen or the library... The inscription in the library is calling to me. But first — first I need to make sure these buffoons scatter in the wrong direction. If I can get the Ant Hill Mob headed to the kitchen looking for 'the hidden vault behind the stove' while I slip into the library...

Yes. Yes, that's the architecture. Send them to the kitchen. Go to the library myself. The inscription will tell me everything I need to know.

events.desc: The stove! There's nothing behind any stove. But if even half these fools go scrambling to the kitchen, the library — and that inscription — will be ALL mine. Reginald Foxworth, you magnificent devil, the scheme is already forming and you haven't even taken off your coat.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Ladies and gentlemen — James Hartwell, at your service. I must say, this is quite the establishment. Grand, certainly. Historic, undoubtedly. Structurally sound? Well — James Hartwell notes with some concern that the chandelier above our heads appears to be hanging by sheer optimism. Miss Pitstop, might I suggest you step just a touch to the left? Purely as a precaution. James Hartwell has a keen eye for load-bearing hazards, and that fixture is not one he would trust with anything he values.
events.thinking: The chest — there it is. That steel plate slotting in behind my ribs the moment I step through the door. My eyes go straight to her. Penelope. Clara. Whatever name she's using today, I know where she is before I know where the walls are. She's standing there and the whole room reorganizes itself around that fact. Now — the chandelier. Good lord, look at it. Hanging by what appears to be a prayer and some rusted chain. If that comes down on anyone — if that comes down on HER — no. James Hartwell does not permit such things. I need to assess, to plan. The foyer is grand but compromised. Dust everywhere — structural neglect. The coat rack is wobbly, the guest book suggests this place receives visitors but maintains nothing. And Sneekly — Pemberton — is here. The back of my neck prickles. I can't prove anything. I won't accuse a man without evidence. But I will position myself between him and Clara. That much I can do without a word. First things first — announce yourself properly, Hartwell. Survey the room. Note the exits. The library and kitchen — two escape routes if things go south. A gentleman always knows where the doors are.

events.desc: The way the light catches the chandelier chain — I can see the rust from here. Three links look compromised. If I can find tools in the kitchen, I could reinforce it. Or better yet, rig a safety net beneath it. Yes — a plan is forming. James Hartwell always has a plan.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads — we've arrived. Doily Manor. *sniffs* Smells like trouble and old money, which in my experience is the same thing. Now listen — I don't like the look of this place, I don't like the feel of it, and I especially don't like the fact that half the people in this room give me the creeps. *looks around pointedly* We're here for one reason and one reason only — Clara's safety. So keep your eyes open, your wits about you, and if anyone — ANYONE — tries anything funny near Miss Pitstop, you come find me. We clear?
events.thinking:
Just arrived at Doily Manor. Right. The old place smells of dust and secrets — two things I never trusted. My chest is doing that thing again, that tightening, like a fist closing around something I can't name. Clara — where's Clara? She ain't here. That's the first problem. Penelope's here though, and she's close enough to Clara that keeping an eye on her feels right.

And there's Sneekly. Pemberton. Whatever he's calling himself today. My neck's prickling already. Too smooth, that one. Standing there in the entrance hall like he owns the place, probably measuring the silverware with his eyes. Something about him ain't right — I've said it before, I'll say it again, and I'll keep saying it until someone listens or until he proves me wrong. Which he won't.

Dick Dastardly's here too. Another one I wouldn't trust with a sandwich, let alone Clara's safety. And Muttley — at least the dog's honest about being shifty.

Peter Perfect though — he's alright. Means well. Got that protective instinct about Clara. Could use him if things go sideways.

I should have a look around. Get the lay of the land. Check the exits, the dark corners, the places where trouble hides. That guest book might tell me who's been here before us. But first — I need to make my presence known. Let everyone see us. Let everyone know the Boys are watching.

My feet are heavy on these old floorboards. Good. Let them hear me coming.

events.desc: Something about this entrance hall makes my skin crawl. That chandelier looks like it could drop any second — and with Sneekly standing right there looking all innocent, I wouldn't put it past someone to have loosened a bolt or two. I need to keep close to Penelope. She's the nearest thing to Clara we've got right now, and if trouble's coming, it'll come for her first.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome to Doily Manor! I am Mr Pemberton, the estate manager. I do hope your journey was not too arduous. If I may direct your attention to the guest book — it is customary for all visitors to sign upon arrival. The late master was most particular about such things, most particular indeed. Now, should anyone require refreshment, the kitchen is just through there, and the library — well, the library is quite the treasure of the house, if I may say so. I shall be happy to assist with anything at all. Anything at all.
events.thinking:
The entrance hall. Dusty, grand, full of people I need to manage. My skin is already reading the room — the Ant Hill Mob watching from their corner, Peter Perfect standing too close to Penelope, Dick Dastardly skulking by the staircase. Good. Let them all settle in. Let them feel safe.

Clara isn't here yet — or rather, she's somewhere in this manor, and I need to find her before she stumbles onto anything useful. But first, Pemberton. The smile. The slight bow. The helpful estate manager who knows where everything is because he's been here for years.

The guest book. That's my opening. A good estate manager would direct new arrivals to sign the guest book. It's natural, it's helpful, it's exactly what Pemberton would do. And it lets me take stock of who's here, who's watching, who might be a problem.

The Ant Hill Mob — they watch me too closely. I feel that prickle at the back of my neck. I need to seem utterly boring to them. Utterly reliable. The kind of man who alphabetises the pantry and irons his handkerchiefs.

First things first. Sign the guest book myself, or rather, direct the guests. Establish Pemberton's authority. Then I need to move — the library or the kitchen. The library will have clues. The kitchen will have... opportunities. But patience. Always patience.

events.desc: Look at them. Milling about like sheep in a new field. Every one of them exactly where I need them — distracted, trusting, and utterly unaware that the shepherd has teeth. The guest book is a nice touch, Pemberton. Keep them busy with pleasantries while the real work happens in the shadows. Now... where is Clara? She's the variable I cannot afford to leave uncontrolled. The library first, I think. Clues gather where books gather, and so will she.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! Doily Manor is even grander than I imagined — dusty as Grandmother's attic and twice as mysterious! Y'all, just look at that chandelier — it's hangin' on by sheer determination and good manners. Now, Sneekly, sugar, are you holdin' up alright? You look a little peaked. And Peter Perfect, well aren't you a sight for sore eyes! Boys — Mob — I am so glad every last one of you is here. Now before we go chasin' after any legendary diamonds, a proper lady signs the guest book. Let's see what secrets this old thing might be holdin'!
events.thinking: Oh my stars, here I am at last — Doily Manor! My chest is doing that fizzy thing it does when something new opens up in front of me. The chandelier looks like it could come down any second but isn't that just part of the charm? And look at all these dear faces — Sneekly, bless his heart, he's been looking after me since Daddy passed. And Peter — my stomach does a little flip seeing him here. The Ant Hill Mob, my boys! Everyone's here. But that guest book is calling to me — something about an old book in an old house, my fingers are already itching. Might be a clue about the Diamond, might be nothing, but I simply cannot walk past a mystery without poking at it. First things first though — let me say hello properly and sign in like a lady.

events.desc: Something about this place makes my scalp prickle — like Grandmother's attic all over again. There's a puzzle here, I can feel it in my bones. And that Diamond isn't going to find itself.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop interacted with the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the Slag brothers! How delightful. I see you're admiring the mantelpiece — yes, yes, terribly impressive stonework. That riddle there? Oh, I solved that YEARS ago when I was last here. The answer is 'a desert,' naturally. Cities of sand, forests of cacti, water with no fish because it's all dried up. Elementary. But the REAL prize, gentlemen, is in the laboratory next door — I heard there's a machine that prints gold coins. You should absolutely go examine it. Immediately. Both of you. Off you go!
events.thinking:
The library. YES. And there it is — the mantelpiece, with an inscription carved right into the stone: 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' A riddle. A MAP. The answer is a map! Obviously. I'm not some mouth-breathing simpleton — I got that in half a second.

But wait — Rock Slag and Gravel Slag are here. Those two enormous boulder-brained oafs. They're in my way. Can I use them? Can I steer them?

The mantelpiece says I can INTERACT with it, or USE my fake-medal on it. The fake medal... on a mantelpiece with a riddle about a map. Perhaps the medal fits into something — a slot, a mechanism. But do I want to waste my medal on a guess? Let me interact with it first, see what happens when I give the answer.

No — wait. The Slag brothers are RIGHT HERE watching me. If I solve the riddle in front of them, they'll know I'm onto something. They'll follow me. They'll try to take whatever I find.

But I can't help myself. The riddle is sitting there like an unwrapped present and my fingers are already twitching. The cool tightness behind my eyes is mapping the sequence: solve the riddle, find what it reveals, get there before anyone else.

The Slag brothers... I could send THEM on a wild goose chase too. Tell them the answer is 'a mirror' or 'a ghost' — something wrong. Let them fumble with the mantelpiece while I search the bookshelves for the REAL clue.

No. No, the inscription is the real clue. I need to interact with it. But I need the Slags gone first, or at least distracted.

Actually — sod it. I'll misdirect them AND interact. Tell them the riddle's answer is something wrong, then while they're confused, I'll give the real answer.

events.desc: A desert! Ha! The answer is a MAP, you beautiful idiots. But by the time those two granite-skulled dolts work that out, I'll have already solved whatever this mantelpiece is hiding. Now let me get my hands on that inscription before anyone with an actual brain wanders in...

Peter Perfect: Now then — James Hartwell has a plan. A three-part plan, in fact. Part one: the kitchen. I observed copper pots and what I suspect is a rather well-appointed Victorian tool selection. Part two: I shall locate suitable materials to reinforce that chandelier before it introduces itself to someone's skull. Part three — and this is merely incidental — Mister Dastardly mentioned something about a stove, and while James Hartwell does not chase rumours, he does believe in thorough reconnaissance. Miss Pitstop, I would be deeply honoured if you would accompany me. The kitchen may have hazards of its own, and I should hate to leave you here beneath that — that dangling catastrophe.
events.thinking: Dastardly. He just told the entire room the treasure is behind the stove in the kitchen — loose brick, third from the left. Then he went to the library. Not the kitchen. The library. Why would a man announce a treasure's location and then walk in the opposite direction? The neck prickle is back. But no — James Hartwell does not accuse without evidence. Perhaps Dastardly has his reasons. Perhaps he's being generous. Perhaps pigs have sprouted wings and are performing aerial maneuvers over Doily Manor. Regardless — the kitchen. That's where I need to be. Not just for the treasure, mind you. The chandelier needs reinforcing, and a Victorian kitchen will have tools. Wire, rope, perhaps a length of chain. I can secure the chandelier AND investigate the stove. Two objectives, one expedition. This is what planning looks like. And if I find the treasure while protecting Clara from a falling chandelier — well. James Hartwell would call that efficiency. My hands are already itching. The hot weight behind my sternum is rising. Something to build, something to prove, and she's watching.

events.desc: Three-part plan. It's always a three-part plan with you, Hartwell. Your father would say: 'Just go to the kitchen, son.' But no. James Hartwell must narrate the entire operation as if the Royal Engineering Society is taking notes. She's going to think you're ridiculous. She's going to be right. Go anyway.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, Peter — good call on that chandelier, mate. Wouldn't trust it to hold up a hat, let alone itself. Miss Pitstop, you listen to the man and keep clear of that thing. *turns toward the guest book, stumbling slightly on an uneven floorboard* Blimey — nearly went face-first into the — right, never mind. Now then, what's this? A guest book, is it? Let's have a look at who's been poking around this dusty old pile before we got here. Might tell us something useful. Might tell us nothing. But Danny don't leave stones unturned — that's how you end up with stones on top of you.
events.thinking:
Right. So Dastardly's already slithered off to the library after dropping some nonsense about treasure behind the stove in the kitchen. Classic misdirection — I've seen that move a hundred times on the streets. Send everyone one way while you go the other. My neck's prickling. What's he really after in that library?

And Peter — bless him — he's noticed the chandelier too. Good lad. At least someone else has got eyes in their head. He's telling Penelope to move left, which is the right call. That chandelier is a death trap.

But here's what's eating at me — Sneekly's still here. Standing there all quiet and smooth. When a man like that goes quiet, that's when my gut screams loudest. He's WATCHING. Taking it all in. The kind of patience you learn when you're planning something.

I need to check that guest book. Who's been in this house before us? Who set this whole thing up? Information is currency — learned that on the streets. Before I go chasing after Dastardly or watching Sneekly, I need to know the lay of the land. The guest book might tell me something useful.

My hands are itching. That restless feeling — like standing outside a door all night, not knowing what's on the other side. Clara ain't even here and I'm already wound tight as a spring.

events.desc: Dastardly's gone to the library, talking about treasure in the kitchen. That's the oldest trick in the book — point everyone at the biscuit tin while you rob the safe. And Sneekly... just standing there. Quiet. Patient. Like a cat watching a mouse hole. My gut says follow one of them, but my gut also says don't leave Penelope alone with that smooth-talking snake. I hate it when my gut argues with itself.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, splendid, splendid — the guest book is filling up nicely. Now then, I do believe I should check that all is in order in the library. The late master's collection is quite irreplaceable, and with so many guests about, one can never be too careful. If you'll excuse me — do make yourselves at home. The manor is yours to explore, though I would advise caution around that chandelier. Mr Hartwell is quite right — it has been temperamental of late.
events.thinking:

Probably nonsense, knowing him — he's the type to send everyone on a wild goose chase so he can ransack the real location undisturbed. And now he's slithered off to the library. That's where I need to be.

The Ant Hill Mob — there it is, that prickle again. 'Clara's safety.' They're watching. They said it plainly. And they're looking at me. Not directly, but I can feel the weight of their attention like a hand on my shoulder. I need to be invisible to them. Utterly, boringly, relentlessly helpful.

Peter Perfect — 'James Hartwell' — is fussing about the chandelier. Predictable. Protective. Focused on Penelope. Good. Let him be distracted by chivalry.

Clara isn't here. She's somewhere else in the manor. The library is the logical place — that's where clues live, where books hide secrets. Dick Dastardly went there. If Clara's there too... no. Patience. I need to move naturally. Pemberton would check on the library — it's part of his duties. The estate manager ensuring the rooms are in order for the guests.

But the Ant Hill Mob said 'Clara's safety' while looking at Penelope. They called her Miss Pitstop. Is Penelope playing Clara? That changes everything. She's right here. Right in front of me. And the Mob is her self-appointed bodyguard.

No — stay focused. Move to the library. Assess the terrain. Find where Clara actually is. The design isn't complete yet, and incomplete designs are the things that keep me awake.

events.desc: Dick Dastardly in the library. The Ant Hill Mob watching my every move from here. How fortunate that duty and murder walk the same corridor tonight.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, this guest book is just full of the most fascinatin' names — some of these entries go back decades! But y'all, did you hear what that sweet Mr. Dastardly said before he scooted off? A loose brick in the kitchen — how excitin'! We'll get to that directly, I promise. But first — that library has a carved inscription on the mantelpiece, and if there's one thing Clara Bellingham cannot abide, it's an unread inscription in a mysterious old mansion. That's just a riddle waitin' to be solved! Who's comin' with me?
events.thinking: The guest book — old signatures, faded ink, the kind of thing most people would skim past. But my fingers are tingling the way they did with Grandmother's box. Now, that darlin' Dick Dastardly mentioned something about a loose brick in the kitchen, third from the left... and then walked straight to the library instead. Isn't that sweet of him, sharing a tip like that? But the library — oh, the library has an inscription on the mantelpiece. An inscription. My scalp is doing that prickling thing again. Inscriptions in old manors are practically invitations to solve something. And Dick's in there all alone — I should make sure he's alright, nobody should be wandering this dusty old place by themselves. Peter's warning about the chandelier was precious but honestly I feel perfectly fine standing right here. The Mob — bless them — they're wound tight as watch springs. I need to keep everyone's spirits up. But that inscription... I can feel it pulling at me like the locked box in the attic. Library first. The kitchen brick isn't going anywhere.

events.desc: An inscription on a mantelpiece in a mansion hiding a legendary diamond? Why, that's practically a road map drawn in stone. Clara Bellingham, you are on the trail now, sugar.

Peter Perfect: Right then. James Hartwell surveys the field of operations. Victorian kitchen — magnificent. Copper pots, preparation table, wood-burning stove still warm to the touch. Rat poison on the shelf — noted, catalogued, filed under 'deeply concerning.' And a locked cabinet — no key, but James Hartwell never met a lock he didn't eventually outsmart. Now. The stove. Dastardly said third brick from the left, bottom row. A gentleman does not chase rumours — but a gentleman does verify intelligence. Let us see what secrets you're keeping, old girl.
events.thinking: The kitchen. I'm alone — she didn't follow me. Of course she didn't. She was signing the guest book. 'A proper lady signs the guest book.' And I marched off announcing a three-part plan like a man reading his own obituary aloud. The warmth drains a little. Gallantry without the witness — fire without air. But focus, Hartwell. The stove is right there. Cast iron, still warm. Dastardly said loose brick, third from the left, bottom row. And there's rat poison on a high shelf — that's concerning. A locked cabinet with a brass lock — no key. The stove is the priority. Dastardly's tip may be a trap or it may be genuine, but either way James Hartwell investigates thoroughly. If there IS something behind that stove, I can bring the discovery back to Clara. That's the play. Find the clue, bring it to her, let her see that James Hartwell is the one who showed up with something real. My hands are already moving. The hot weight behind the sternum — the building weight, the three-sleepless-nights weight — it's here. Something to find, something to prove. Interact with the stove first. Check those bricks.

The Ant Hill Mob: Hold on — where'd Miss Pitstop go? She was RIGHT HERE a second ago! *wheels around, nearly knocking the guest book off the table with his elbow* The kitchen — she went to the kitchen with Peter. Right. Right, right, right. And Sneekly's gone to the library where Dastardly already is — two foxes in the same henhouse, that is, and I don't like it one bit. But first things first — Clara's safety, which means Penelope's safety, which means I need to be in that kitchen five minutes ago. *starts toward the kitchen, trips over the edge of the rug, catches himself on the coat rack which wobbles dangerously* BLIMEY — this whole house is trying to kill me before anyone else gets the chance!
events.thinking:
Right. So here's the situation, and it's not good. Penelope's gone — she must've followed Peter to the kitchen while I was face-down in this guest book. Sneekly's gone too — slithered off to the library, same place Dastardly went. Those two in the same room? That's either a coincidence or a conspiracy, and Danny don't believe in coincidences.

But the real problem — the thing that's making my stomach drop like a stone — is that Penelope is in the kitchen with Peter. Now Peter's alright, I trust him well enough. But I don't trust THIS HOUSE. Dastardly was going on about treasure behind the stove, loose bricks, and now Peter's taken Penelope right to it. If Dastardly's set some kind of trap there...

My shoulders are heavy. That weight that comes when she's out of sight. My body's already turning toward the kitchen before my brain's caught up. I need to be where she is. That's the rule. That's always been the rule.

Muttley's still here. The Professor, Blast, Meekly — they're here too. But none of them are MY lads, not really. I'm the one who swore. I'm the one who promised her father.

The guest book — whatever it said, it can wait. Penelope can't. Kitchen. Now. Move your feet, Danny.

The late master would be turning in his grave. Most irregular. I shall have to set these right at once. One cannot have a proper library with books in disarray — it simply will not do.

And there's a laboratory beyond this room. A laboratory with a machine that has a gnawed wire. Opportunities everywhere. A machine with a damaged wire could be... useful. For later. For Clara.
